title: Patch Notes
description: Write a prompt that gets an AI to turn a messy list of changes into player-facing patch notes.
scenario: Your indie studio ships a balance update to its online card game tonight. The engineers left a bullet list of 14 changes written for other engineers (ticket numbers, internal card codenames, no context). Players need patch notes they can actually read: what changed, why, and what it means for their decks.
targetOutput: Patch notes with a short summary, grouped sections (balance, bug fixes, quality of life), one line per change in player language, and a note on anything that affects ranked play.

evaluationCriteria.description: Does the prompt say who reads the notes and what they care about?

evaluationCriteria.name: Structure
evaluationCriteria.description: Does it ask for sections and a summary?

evaluationCriteria.name: Translation
evaluationCriteria.description: Does it tell the AI to replace internal names and ticket numbers with player terms?

evaluationCriteria.name: Tone
evaluationCriteria.description: Does it set a tone (clear, friendly, no hype)?

evaluationCriteria.name: Completeness
evaluationCriteria.description: Does it insist every change is covered?

evaluationCriteria.name: Clarity
evaluationCriteria.description: Is the prompt itself unambiguous?

Turn the change list below into patch notes: start with a three-sentence summary, then sections for Balance, Bug fixes and Quality of life. One line per change, in plain language, with the reason in parentheses. Replace internal card codenames with the public card names from the glossary I provide. Flag anything that changes ranked play with [Ranked].
